_note: English version of the apprentice safety induction (commun.json, mpi.json, etancheur.json). Same ids; answers in the SAME ORDER as the French file (the first one is the right answer). Plain English for learners.

C0-1.q: I am an apprentice. The school rules:
r: apply to me, like to all students
only concern full-time students
only apply during lesson time
C0-1.e: An apprentice at the training centre is inside the school. The same rules apply to him, at the same times.

C0-2.q: I arrive late at the training centre. I:
r: go to the school office first, then I go in
go straight in, my employer has been told
stay in the corridor until the end of the lesson
C0-2.e: Being late always goes through the school office. That is the school rule, apprentice or not.

C0-3.q: I am absent on a training-centre day. I tell:
r: the training centre and my employer, both
only my employer, he will pass it on
only the training centre, it will pass it on
C0-3.e: An apprentice has two places. An absence must be justified on both sides, with a paper.

C0-4.q: During a lesson at the training centre, my phone is:
r: in my bag, on silent
in my pocket, on vibrate
on the table, screen down
C0-4.e: The phone stays in the bag. It comes out only if the trainer asks, for example to take a photo of a plan.

C0-5.q: The fire alarm rings during the lesson. I:
r: go out with the group, without taking anything
take my things, then go out with the group
wait to find out if it is a drill
C0-5.e: You leave at once, without taking anything, and you stay with the group: that is where people are counted.

C0-6.q: Leaving the school between two lessons:
r: follows what the school rules allow
is free for an apprentice over 18
is free if I send a message to the school office
C0-6.e: The school rules say who can go out and when. If in doubt, ask the school office.

C1-1.q: I know I will be late at my employer's. I:
r: call him before my start time
explain when I arrive on site
tell my supervisor at the end of the day
C1-1.e: Calling before is what makes the difference between being late and leaving your job.

C1-2.q: My supervisor gives an instruction I did not understand. I:
r: ask him to repeat it straight away
do what I think and see later
ask another apprentice on site
C1-2.e: Asking is not a weakness. A badly understood instruction ends in work to redo, or in an accident.

C1-3.q: I am asked to do a job I have never learned. I:
r: tell my supervisor before I start
try anyway, that is how you learn
refuse and leave the site
C1-3.e: An apprentice learns with someone. A task you don't know is done with someone, never alone.

r: can be completely forbidden by the company
is allowed at lunch, in small amounts
is allowed away from the machines
C1-4.e: The company rules can forbid it completely. And a worker who has been drinking is taken off the job.

C1-5.q: I want to post a photo of the site on social media. I:
r: first ask my employer for permission
post it, the site can be seen from the street
post it if nobody is in the picture
C1-5.e: The site, the customer and the company do not belong to me. You ask before you post.

r: is given free by the employer
is paid by me, like my everyday clothes
is shared between the apprentices
C2-1.e: The law says so: the employer gives it, looks after it and replaces it, and you pay nothing.

C2-2.q: My helmet has taken a hit. I:
r: report it, the company replaces it
keep going, the shell is not broken
keep it and I am more careful
C2-2.e: A helmet that has taken a hit does not protect any more. It is replaced, never repaired.

C2-3.q: I am missing a piece of protective equipment. I:
r: ask for it before starting work
borrow one from another apprentice in the team
start and get it later
C2-3.e: Without the equipment, the work does not start. Asking for it is part of the job.

r: only me, and only if I wear it
the whole team working around me
me, even when it is left in the van
C2-4.e: Personal means: only me. Left in the van or badly worn, it protects nobody.

C3-1.q: An apprentice under 18 works at height:
r: if collective protection is in place (guardrail, platform)
if he wears a harness and is trained
if a colleague stays with him on the ground
C3-1.e: The law says it: without collective protection, a minor does not go up. A special permission exists, under strict rules.

C3-2.q: Putting up or taking down scaffolding, under 18:
r: is forbidden without a declared special permission
is allowed if a trained colleague is with me
is allowed if my supervisor is watching
C3-2.e: It is regulated work. The employer must declare a special permission to the labour inspectorate.

C3-3.q: Between a guardrail and a harness, you first put up:
r: the guardrail, which protects everybody
the harness, which is much quicker to put on
whichever one the boss has to hand
C3-3.e: Collective protection comes before personal protection: it even protects the person who forgets.

C3-4.q: The scaffolding was already up yesterday. This morning:
r: we check it: platform, guardrails, base
we look at the date on the inspection tag
we go up, it has not moved during the night
C3-4.e: This is the daily check of the scaffolding. One windy night or someone passing is enough to change it.

C3-5.q: I wear a harness. I clip it on:
r: an anchor point made for that
the strongest bar around
the frame of the scaffolding
C3-5.e: An anchor point is designed to hold a fall. Any old bar is not.

C5-1.q: I break a customer's window during the job:
r: my employer is responsible, and I tell him
I pay for the window from my wages
the customer turns to the training centre and the school
C5-1.e: The employer is responsible for damage caused by his apprentice while he supervises him.

C5-2.q: I caused some damage and nobody saw it. I:
r: tell my supervisor before I leave
wait for someone to ask me
repair it myself without saying anything
C5-2.e: Hidden damage is found later and costs more. Telling protects the company and me.

C5-3.q: Damage done on purpose, for fun or in anger:
r: is paid by me, the employer does not cover it
is covered like any other damage
is covered by the school insurance
C5-3.e: The employer covers the work, not something done on purpose.

C5-4.q: I cut my finger on site, it is not serious. I:
r: tell my supervisor straight away
finish the day and see
put a plaster on and carry on
C5-4.e: A small injury that is not reported becomes a problem if it gets infected. You always tell someone.

C5-5.q: After an accident, I tell my employer within:
r: 24 hours
one week
48 hours
C5-5.e: Twenty-four hours: that is the time written in the law. After that, everything becomes harder.

C5-6.q: My employer reports the accident to the Social Security within:
r: 48 hours
24 hours
15 days
C5-6.e: Forty-eight hours, not counting Sundays and bank holidays. The employer fills in the form.

C5-7.q: The work-accident form is used to:
r: get medical care without paying
justify my absence at the training centre
get my wages during sick leave
C5-7.e: With this form, the doctor and the chemist do not ask for money. The employer gives it to me.

C5-8.q: I get hurt during a lesson at the training centre:
r: it is a work accident, like at the company
it is a school accident, not a work accident
it depends on my age and my contract
C5-8.e: An apprentice is covered from the first day: at the company, at the training centre, and on the way there.

M-1.q: I sand the joints of a ceiling. I protect myself:
r: with a sander with dust extraction and an FFP2 mask
with a cloth mask and the window open
by wetting the surface before sanding
M-1.e: Plaster contains a little silica. You extract the dust at the source, and an FFP2 mask is the minimum.

r: by two people, or with a board lifter
alone, held flat at my side
alone, on my shoulder
M-2.e: A board is heavy and awkward. Two people or a board lifter: your back cannot be repaired.

M-3.q: I cut a board with a utility knife. I:
r: cut with the hand holding the rule out of the way
pull the blade towards me to see the line better
put the board on my knees to hold it
M-3.e: The blade always moves away from the body, and the hand holding the rule stays out of its path.

M-4.q: To screw a ceiling, I stand on:
r: a platform with guardrails
a stepladder on two trestles
a ladder held by a friend
M-4.e: A platform with guardrails keeps both hands free and stops a fall.

M-5.q: I install mineral wool insulation. I wear:
r: gloves, long sleeves and a mask
only handling gloves
only safety glasses
M-5.e: The fibres irritate the skin, the eyes and the throat. You cover up, and you never work bare-chested.

M-6.q: The saw has lost its blade guard. I:
r: do not use it and tell my supervisor
use it, being very, very careful
put the guard back with tape
M-6.e: A tool without its guard is put aside. You never repair a safety device yourself.

M-7.q: To clean plaster dust on the floor, I use:
r: a vacuum cleaner with a filter, not a broom
the broom, it is much faster
the air blower on the compressor
M-7.e: A broom or an air blower puts the dust back in the air, where you breathe. The vacuum keeps it.

M-8.q: At the end of the job, the plasterboard offcuts:
r: go into the skip for plaster
go with the ordinary site waste
stay on site for the next team
M-8.e: Plaster is sorted on its own. Mixed with other waste, it cannot be recycled and it costs more.

E-1.q: Before using a torch (flame) on a roof, you need:
r: a signed hot-work permit before starting
the site manager's spoken OK on the spot
a spare gas bottle on the roof
E-1.e: The hot-work permit is signed before any work with a flame. It says who watches, and with what equipment.

E-2.q: At the torch work area, the fire extinguisher is:
r: within reach, checked before starting
at the bottom of the access ladder
in the team's van, parked in front of the building
E-2.e: One ABC powder extinguisher for each hot-work area, checked at the start of every shift.

E-3.q: Stored propane bottles are kept away from insulation, at:
r: at least 10 metres
at least 2 metres
at least 5 metres
E-3.e: Ten metres between stored bottles and anything that can burn, insulation panels included.

E-4.q: On a flat roof, the access points must:
r: stay clear, to get out in an emergency
be locked to keep intruders out
also be used to store materials
E-4.e: A fire can block one way out. You need two, clear and ready to use at once.

E-5.q: Against splashes of hot bitumen, I wear:
r: gauntlet gloves and long trousers
short gloves, easier in summer
cloth handling gloves
E-5.e: Hot bitumen sticks to the skin and keeps burning. Gauntlets, long sleeves, high safety boots.

E-6.q: I have bitumen on my skin. I take it off:
r: with a skin-cleaning cream, never with solvent
with thinner from the site, it is quicker
by scraping it once it is hard
E-6.e: Solvent attacks the skin and pushes the product in. You clean with a skin-cleaning cream.

E-7.q: I must work at the edge of a flat roof with no high parapet:
r: the guardrail goes up before starting
staying one metre from the edge is enough
the harness can go on after the first upstand
E-7.e: Nothing starts before the edge is protected. Being careful is not a protection.

E-8.q: The torch is off, the day is over. The work area:
r: is watched for a while before leaving the site
can be left, the torch is really off
is just sprayed with site water
E-8.e: A hidden fire can start after everyone has left. The hot-work permit says who watches, and until when.
